name: ForeFlight
subcategory: aviation flight planning / electronic flight bag
tagline: Flight planning, charts, weather and in-cockpit navigation for pilots, on iPad and iPhone.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: It is true that a lot of what ForeFlight shows is government data: FAA airport records, NOAA weather, raster sectionals, published procedures. It is also true that an agent can build you a decent VFR route planner with wind triangle math, METARs and a moving map in a weekend. What it cannot build is a navigation data pipeline that is correct on every 28 day AIRAC cycle, georeferenced approach plates and Jeppesen coverage outside the US, ADS-B and avionics integration, or the operational track record that gets an app accepted as an electronic flight bag under Part 91 and 135. The failure mode here is not a bad user experience, it is being wrong about terrain, an obstacle or a runway while airborne with no cell signal. Build the planner for fun, keep the subscription for flying.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that plans a VFR route between airports using free FAA and NOAA data, computes headings, groundspeed, ETE and fuel on each leg, and draws it on a cached sectional map.
requirements: Internet access to fetch FAA NASR airport data and aviationweather.gov products
Disk space for cached raster chart tiles
Your aircraft performance numbers entered by hand
whatYouLose: Current, cycle-accurate navigation data and georeferenced instrument approach plates
ADS-B in traffic and weather, plus panel integration with Garmin and Avidyne avionics
Filing and activating flight plans, plus logbook, weight and balance and performance profiles that people actually trust
Offline reliability on a tablet in a cockpit, which is the only condition that matters
moatNotes: The data is public until it is not: procedure plates, terrain, obstacles and non-US charting all come with licensing and update obligations that a hobby project will quietly get wrong.
whyPeopleStillPay: Pilots pay because the app is part of a safety-critical workflow that is inspected, audited and occasionally used as evidence. Currency matters more than features: charts and navdata refresh on a fixed cycle, and being one cycle stale is a real problem, not a cosmetic one. Add hardware pairing, avionics sync, flight plan filing and the fact that everyone at the flight school and the flight department already uses it, and a personal clone stops being a replacement and becomes a toy you check on the ground.
notes: A wind triangle is an afternoon; a current nav database is not. The moat is licensed chart and navigation data pipelines plus the regulatory acceptance that lets you actually fly with it.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user VFR flight planning web app called Preflight. Ground use only, planning aid, not for navigation.

Stack, no substitutions:
- TypeScript everywhere, pnpm, one repo
- Vite + React + MapLibre GL JS for the UI
- Fastify server for data fetching, caching and math
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for airports and cached weather
- No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics. Runs on localhost.

Data, all free and keyless:
- Airports, runways and frequencies: download the FAA NASR subscription CSV files at startup via a `pnpm run seed` script, load into SQLite, log the effective cycle date visibly in the UI
- Weather: aviationweather.gov data API for METAR, TAF and winds/temps aloft, cached in SQLite with a fetched-at timestamp
- Basemap: OpenStreetMap raster tiles through a local disk tile cache directory; make the tile URL template a .env value so a sectional chart tile source can be swapped in

Features in scope:
- Route entry as identifiers, e.g. KBED KASH KCON, with optional lat/lon waypoints
- Aircraft profiles: name, true airspeed, fuel burn per hour, usable fuel, plus a simple weight and balance table with arms and moment limits, all stored in SQLite and editable in the UI
- Per-leg computation: great circle distance in nautical miles, true course, magnetic course using a local magnetic declination model, wind correction angle and groundspeed from winds aloft at the chosen altitude, ETE, fuel burned and fuel remaining
- A printable nav log table and a route line drawn on the map with airport markers
- A weather strip showing METAR and TAF for departure, destination and any alternate, with raw text always visible next to any decoded version
- Persistent banner: data cycle date, weather fetch time, and the words "planning aid only, not for navigation"

Explicitly out of scope, do not fake these:
- Instrument approach plates, georeferenced charts, IFR procedures, airways
- NOTAM decoding, TFRs, airspace boundary checks, terrain or obstacle alerting
- Filing or activating flight plans, ADS-B, any live position tracking
- Mobile apps and offline tablet use

Deliverables: working app, `pnpm seed` then `pnpm dev`, a .env.example with the tile URL template, unit tests for the wind triangle and weight and balance math with hand-checked values, and a README that states plainly what this cannot be used for.
